title: Minimal primes of a parameter product in a strict henselization
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $x_1,\ldots,x_r$, $r\geq0$, be members at distinct positions of a regular system of parameters of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters], and let $H$ be a strict henselization of $A$ relative to a separable closure of $A/\mathfrak m$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Write $x_i$ also for its image in $H$, put $F=\prod_{i=1}^r x_i$, and put $P_i=x_iH$. Each $H/P_i$ is a regular local ring and a nonzero integral domain. The $P_i$ are proper prime ideals and are pairwise incomparable: for $i\neq j$, $x_i\notin P_j$. The primes of $H$ minimal over $(F)$ are exactly $P_1,\ldots,P_r$. Thus the reduced ring $(H/(F))_{\mathrm{red}}$ has exactly $r$ minimal prime ideals, namely the images of these $P_i$, where reduction means quotient by the ideal of all nilpotent elements and a minimal prime means a prime minimal under inclusion. If $r\geq1$, $H/(F)$ is a strict henselization of $A/(F)$ with its induced residue-field choice; every strict henselization of $A/(F)$ with that residue-field choice has a reduction with exactly $r$ minimal primes. If $r=0$, $F=1$, $H/(F)$ is the zero ring and has no prime ideals.

source.place: Local algebra for ILO Expose VIII 4.1.6 (printed p.118): Tags 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization), 00NP (lemma-regular-domain), 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective); more-algebra.tex Tags 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular) and 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), part (1).

proof.text: If $r=0$, the empty product is $F=1$. Thus $(F)=H$, $H/(F)=0$, and there is no proper prime ideal containing $(F)$ or in this quotient. Every assertion indexed by $i$ is vacuous, so this proves the empty case. In the remaining steps assume $r\geq1$.

source.place: Empty-product convention and the definition of a prime ideal.

proof.text: Choose a full regular system $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $A$ containing the marked positions. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular], $H$ is regular local (the Noetherian hypothesis holds because $A$ is regular local). By [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal], its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak mH=(t_1,\ldots,t_d)H$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], $\dim H=\dim A=d$. Consequently the image list $(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$ is a regular system of parameters of $H$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]; the marked positions remain distinct.

source.place: Tags 06LN (lemma-henselization-regular), 06LK (lemma-henselization-dimension), and 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), part (2); compare the parameter argument in the proof of 06LN.

proof.text: For each $i$, permute the full parameter list of $H$ to put $x_i$ first. [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] with $c=1$ makes $H/P_i$ regular local, and [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes it a nonzero domain. Hence $P_i$ is proper and prime: $ab\in P_i$ implies that one of the classes of $a,b$ is zero in this domain. For $i\ne j$, put $x_j$ first and $x_i$ second in the full list. The same regular-sequence theorem and [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] give injectivity of multiplication by $x_i$ on $H/(x_j)$. If $x_i\in(x_j)$ that multiplication is zero, contradicting injectivity on this nonzero quotient (apply it to $1$ and $0$). Thus $x_i\notin P_j$, which also proves pairwise incomparability.

Each $P_i$ contains $F$. If a prime $Q$ contains $F=\prod_i x_i$, repeated use of the defining prime-ideal implication for a product gives $x_j\in Q$ for some $j$, hence $P_j\subseteq Q$. If $Q\subseteq P_i$ also, then $P_j\subseteq P_i$ forces $j=i$ by the preceding incomparability, and $Q=P_i$. This proves each $P_i$ minimal over $(F)$. Conversely, a prime minimal over $(F)$ contains a $P_j$ and therefore equals it. The $r$ ideals are distinct.

source.place: Elementary prime-ideal argument for a finite product, after 00NQ and 00NP.

proof.text: For any ideal $I$ of a commutative ring $R$, preimage and image under $R\to R/I$ give mutually inverse, inclusion-preserving correspondences between primes of $R/I$ and primes of $R$ containing $I$: the primality test on classes is exactly $ab\in Q\Rightarrow a\in Q$ or $b\in Q$. They therefore preserve minimal primes. Every prime contains every nilpotent element, since $z^n=0$ in a prime implies $z$ lies in it by repeated primality. Apply the correspondence first to $H\to H/(F)$ and then to the quotient of $H/(F)$ by all its nilpotents. The resulting minimal primes are exactly the images of the $P_i$, so the reduction has exactly $r$ minimal primes.

source.place: Elementary ideal correspondence for quotients and the defining prime test; reduction by nilpotents.

proof.text: Since $r\geq1$ and every $x_i\in\mathfrak m$, $I=(F)\subseteq\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $B=A/I$ is nonzero local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$. Its residue field is canonically $A/\mathfrak m$: the map sending the class of the class of $a$ to the class of $a$ is an inverse to the evident map in the other direction. Transport the chosen separable closure $K$ along this identification and apply [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient-core] to the surjection $A\to B$, $C=H$, and this transported choice $L=K$. Its kernel is $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so the lemma gives a $B$-algebra structure on the explicit quotient $H/IH$. Since $IH=(F)H$, this is the required strict henselization $H/(F)$ with the induced residue-field choice.

By [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], any other strict henselization of $B=A/(F)$ relative to the same $K$ is isomorphic as a $B$-algebra to the colimit of the same pointed etale-algebra diagram. The two universal properties give comparison maps in both directions; their composites are identities because their composites with every colimit leg are identities and the universal map is unique. Hence it is $B$-algebra isomorphic to $H/(F)$. A ring isomorphism carries nilpotents to nilpotents and primes to primes, preserving and reflecting inclusion, so it induces a bijection on minimal primes of the reductions. The number is therefore $r$ for every such choice.

source.place: Definition of strict henselization as a universal colimit; uniqueness from its universal property.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of Tags 06LN, 06LK, 07QM(2), Algebra Tags 00NQ, 00NP, 05WS, and the explicit elementary finite-product and quotient-prime arguments.
